meta.source_provenance: Email from PC Jon Dixon to Ben Carter on 7 Nov 2024 at 19:06 (provided by user)

emails.subject_summary: Response: which evidence to upload (calls not needed, videos requested)
emails.body:
Hi Ben
In regard to those calls you mentioned you don’t need to send those for the time being.
Text messages, Call Logs and Voicemails. Please upload any videos, there’s mention of one video of Alanna banging on the door?
Evidence of anything after the time you made it clear to Alanna that you didn’t want any further contact from her is what is most relevant, but anything else fairly recent involving her making any threats or anything you feel is particularly harassing or distressful to yourself.

contradiction_links.claim: Police considered all evidence victim offered.
contradiction_links.reality: Despite victim offering call recordings, police told him not to send them 'for the time being'.
laws_breached: Victims’ Code 2020 (Right to have evidence considered)

events: Police declined to receive call recordings at this stage.
Requested text messages, call logs, voicemails, and especially video evidence of door-banging.
Acknowledged no-contact boundary as reference point for evidence relevance.

damages_summary.strategic: By refusing call recordings, police limited contemporaneous evidence trail.
damages_summary.emotional: Victim may feel dismissed despite proactive evidence offers.
